This process prepares you to write clear learning outcomes and help students make the connection between course expectations, activities, and the competencies that they seek to develop.

content.title: Write clear and measurable learning outcomes.

content.placeholder: While competencies provide examples of the knowledge, skills, or attitudes students can expect to develop during the course, learning outcomes that connect to the required ELAC learning competencies are more specific and measurable goals. Learning outcomes are statements that reflect the action students will take to demonstrate what they have learned. In addition to the required ELAC learning outcomes, you will likely want to articulate a couple of course-specific learning outcomes related to additional competencies of your course. This section guides you through writing course-specific learning outcomes. A clear and measurable learning outcome contains four elements, listed here with corresponding examples:

content.title: Consider who is doing the learning in your course.

content.placeholder: When you write course learning outcomes you should consider who is doing the learning (is it all students in your course, majors in your course, non-majors in your course?). While you may have separate goals for a specific group of students (such as majors) in your course, you should write learning outcomes for all students in your course that will be listed in the syllabus. Second, for course learning outcomes, the learning should take place during the course in question. What should students in your course be able to do by the end of the course? The third and fourth elements require specific articulation of what will be learned and how. Specificity is important so that students can identify what is expected of them during the course.
